minutes.headline: Board added a sixth marijuana ballot question and a marijuana excise article, and tabled a two-night Town Meeting plan.
minutes.summary: The board met the Grange, heard a Complete Streets update, and held a workshop with open space and parks members on reusing TC Passios and conveying the old primary school and Brooks house. It extended the warrant closing date, added marijuana items, extended an earth removal permit and approved a PILOT agreement. It ranked projects for the senator's funding request and tabled the question of a split Town Meeting to March 5.

what_happened.line: The board voted 2-1 to add a sixth marijuana question, on prohibiting marijuana researchers, to the May election ballot.
The board added a warrant article for a local option excise on retail marijuana; the minutes record the vote as not audible.
The board extended the closing of the annual Town Meeting warrant to March 25 at 4:00 p.m., and tabled a two-night Town Meeting question to March 5 with public input.
A workshop on reusing TC Passios and conveying the old primary school and Brooks house drew public comment on offices, green space and leasing rather than selling.
The board will submit its senator funding list with fuel tanks at lowest priority, to be revisited in March.

why_it_matters: The marijuana ballot question and excise article put a local tax and a local rule before voters in May and at Town Meeting.
What happens to TC Passios, the old primary school and the Brooks house sets where town offices go and whether town land is leased or sold, which bears on a possible large building cost to taxpayers.
Whether Town Meeting runs one night or two decides when residents can attend and vote on the budget and warrant articles.
watch_next: March 5 meeting: the board takes up the two-night Town Meeting question with public input.
March 25 at 4:00 p.m.: the annual Town Meeting warrant closes.
